plain_text:
Within the Golden Radio Hour archive, Orson Welles is credited on 150 distinct recordings across 8 programs from 1936-09-19 through 1953-10-04. Documented roles include performer on 113 recordings, narrator on 32 recordings, host on 7 recordings, writer on 3 recordings, radio adaptor on 2 recordings, and director on 2 recordings.

The strongest program connections in the current GRH holdings are The Lives of Harry Lime (performer on 52 recordings and writer on 3 recordings; 52 distinct recordings), The Shadow (performer on 42 recordings; 42 distinct recordings), The Black Museum (narrator on 32 recordings; 32 distinct recordings), The Mercury Theatre on the Air (performer on 14 recordings, host on 5 recordings, radio adaptor on 2 recordings, director on 2 recordings, and producer on 1 recording; 17 distinct recordings), Columbia Workshop (host on 2 recordings and performer on 2 recordings; 4 distinct recordings), Lux Radio Theatre (performer on 1 recording; 1 distinct recording), The Fred Allen Show (performer on 1 recording; 1 distinct recording), and Theatre Royal (performer on 1 recording; 1 distinct recording).

Documented character portrayals include Harry Lime (52 portrayals) and Lamont Cranston / The Shadow (42 portrayals).
